title.zh: 卷370 列傳一百五十七 琦善 伊里布 宗室耆英
title.en: Volume 370 Biographies 157: Qi Shan, Yi Libu, Zong Shiqiying
title.raw: 卷370 列傳一百五十七 琦善 伊里布 宗室耆英

sentences.zh: 琦善 琦善，字靜庵，博爾濟吉特氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Qi Shan. Qi Shan, style name Jing'an, of the Borjigit clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan. Qi Shan, whose style was Jing'an, belonged to the Borjigit clan and came from the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 父成德，熱河都統，以先世格得理爾率屬歸附，世襲一等侯爵。

translations.literal: His father Chengde was military governor of Rehe; because an ancestor Gedriel had led his followers in submission, the family held the hereditary rank of first-class marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengde served as military governor of Rehe. An earlier forebear, Gedriel, had led his people in submitting to the dynasty, and the family thereafter held a hereditary first-class marquisate.

sentences.zh: 琦善由廕生授刑部員外郎，累遷通政司副使。

translations.literal: Qi Shan entered office through the yin privilege as an assistant department director in the Ministry of Punishments, and was promoted in stages to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan began his career through hereditary privilege as an assistant director in the Ministry of Punishments and rose step by step to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十九年，出為河南按察使，歷江寧、河南布政使。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Jiaqing he went out as Henan surveillance commissioner, and served in succession as Jiangning and Henan provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 19 (1814) he was posted as surveillance commissioner of Henan, and later held the provincial treasurerships of Jiangning and Henan in turn.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，擢河南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was promoted to Henan governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 24 (1819) he was promoted to governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 河決馬營壩，偕尚書吳璥督工，甫塞而儀封南岸又決，奪職，予主事銜留工。

translations.literal: When the Yellow River broke through at Maying Dam, he joined Minister Wu Jin in supervising the works; they had just sealed the breach when the south bank at Yifeng broke again. He was stripped of office but given the rank of a department director and kept on the project.
translations.idiomatic: When the river burst the Maying Dam, he worked with Minister Wu Jin to oversee repairs. The breach had barely been closed when the south bank at Yifeng gave way again. He lost his post but was allowed to remain on the works with the nominal rank of a department director.

sentences.zh: 尋授河南按察使，調山東。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Henan surveillance commissioner and transferred to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed surveillance commissioner of Henan and then transferred to Shandong.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，就擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was promoted on the spot to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 1 (1821) he was promoted in place to provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 父憂，奪情任事，襲侯爵。

translations.literal: When his father died he was released from mourning to continue in office and inherited the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: On his father's death he was recalled from mourning to duty and succeeded to the family marquisate.

sentences.zh: 捕治臨清教匪馬進忠，又籌濟高家堰工費八十萬。

translations.literal: He captured and punished the Linqing sect rebel Ma Jinzhong, and also raised eight hundred thousand taels for works at the Gaojiayan embankment.
translations.idiomatic: He captured and dealt with the Linqing sect rebel Ma Jinzhong and raised eight hundred thousand taels to fund repairs at the Gaojiayan embankment.

sentences.zh: 五年，京察，詔嘉其明幹有為，能任勞怨，加總督銜。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, at the capital inspection, an edict praised his clarity, efficiency, and capacity for action, and his willingness to bear hardship and blame; he was given the rank of governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 5 (1825), at the metropolitan personnel review, the throne praised his sharp competence and willingness to shoulder thankless work, and granted him governor-general rank.

sentences.zh: 尋擢兩江總督，兼署漕運總督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to governor-general of the Two Jiangs and also acted as grain-transport governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to governor-general of the Two Jiangs and concurrently served as acting grain-transport governor-general.

sentences.zh: 時高堰屢決，淤運阻漕。

translations.literal: At that time the Gaoyan embankment broke repeatedly, silt choked the transport channel, and grain shipment was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoyan embankment was breaching repeatedly, silt was choking the canal, and grain transport had stalled.

sentences.zh: 琦善請用盤運法，並暫行海運，如議行。

translations.literal: Qi Shan requested the use of relay transport and a temporary shift to sea transport; both measures were adopted as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan proposed relay haulage along with a temporary resort to sea transport, and both plans were put into effect.

sentences.zh: 七年，議啟王家營舊減壩，大濬正河，尋以減壩堵合，黃水倒漾，复閉禦黃壩，漕船倒塘灌放，詔斥失機，議革職，寬之，降授內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year it was decided to reopen the old relief sluice at Wangjiaying and dredge the main channel on a large scale. Soon the relief sluice was sealed again, the Yellow River water surged back, and the Yellow River control dam was closed once more; grain boats were backed into the pond for release by flooding. An edict rebuked him for missing the moment; dismissal was proposed, but he was spared and demoted to a Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 7 (1827) he backed reopening the old Wangjiaying relief sluice and a major dredging of the main channel. Soon the sluice was shut again, Yellow River water backed up, the control dam had to be closed anew, and grain boats had to be floated out by reversing the pond flow. The court rebuked him for losing the opportunity; though dismissal was debated, he was spared and demoted to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 尋复授山東巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was again appointed Shandong governor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reappointed governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢四川總督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to Sichuan governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 9 (1829) he was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 十一年，調直隸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 11 (1831) he was transferred to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 十六年，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he became an associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 16 (1836) he was made associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 十八年，拜文淵閣大學士，仍留總督任。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion while retaining his governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 18 (1838) he was made Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and kept his post as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 琦善久膺疆寄，為宣宗所倚任。

translations.literal: Qi Shan had long held frontier responsibilities and was relied upon by the Daoguang Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan had long borne heavy frontier duties and enjoyed the Daoguang Emperor's trust.

sentences.zh: 二十年，海疆事急，駐天津籌辦防務。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, as the maritime frontier grew urgent, he was stationed at Tianjin to organize coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 20 (1840), with the coastal crisis mounting, he was posted to Tianjin to organize defenses.

sentences.zh: 八月，英兵船至海口，投書乞通商，訴林則徐、鄧廷楨等燒煙啟釁。

translations.literal: In the eighth month British warships reached Haikou, sent a letter requesting trade, and complained that Lin Zexu, Deng Tingzhen, and others had burned opium and provoked hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month British warships reached Haikou, delivered a letter asking to resume trade, and blamed Lin Zexu, Deng Tingzhen, and others for burning opium and starting the conflict.

sentences.zh: 琦善招宴英領事義律及兵官，許以代奏。

translations.literal: Qi Shan invited the British consul Charles Elliot and his officers to a banquet and promised to memorialize on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan entertained the British consul Charles Elliot and his officers and promised to relay their petition to the throne.

sentences.zh: 遂入覲面陳，授欽差大臣，赴廣東查辦。

translations.literal: He then entered the capital for an audience and presented his report in person; he was appointed imperial commissioner and sent to Guangdong to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to court, reported in person, was appointed imperial commissioner, and dispatched to Guangdong to investigate.

sentences.zh: 諭沿海疆吏但防要隘，遇英船毋開砲，義律乃率船回粵。

translations.literal: Coastal officials were instructed to guard only key passes and not to open fire when they met British ships; Elliot then led his fleet back to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal officials were told to hold only the vital passes and not to fire on British vessels; Elliot then took his fleet back to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 尋罷則徐、廷楨，命琦善署兩廣總督兼粵海關監督。

translations.literal: Soon Lin Zexu and Deng Tingzhen were dismissed, and Qi Shan was ordered to act as governor-general of the Two Guangs and superintendent of the Guangdong Customs.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zexu and Deng Tingzhen were soon removed, and Qi Shan was made acting governor-general of the Two Guangs and superintendent of the Guangdong Customs.

sentences.zh: 密疏臚陳粵事，略曰：「林則徐示令繳煙，許以賞犒，洋人頗存奢望。

translations.literal: In a secret memorial he set out the Guangdong situation in detail, saying in summary: 'Lin Zexu ordered surrender of opium and promised rewards; the foreigners entertained high hopes.
translations.idiomatic: In a secret memorial he laid out the Guangdong situation at length, writing in part: 'Lin Zexu ordered the surrender of opium and promised rewards and compensation; the foreigners had come to expect much.

sentences.zh: 迨後每煙一箱，僅給茶葉五斤，所得不及本銀百分之一；

translations.literal: Later, for each chest of opium they were given only five catties of tea, yielding less than one percent of the original silver value;
translations.idiomatic: Later they received only five catties of tea per chest—less than one percent of what the opium had cost them;

sentences.zh: 又勒具'再販船貨入官、人即正法'甘結，迄未遵依，此釁所由起也。

translations.literal: they were also forced to submit a written pledge that any renewed trafficking in goods would be confiscated and the person immediately executed, which they have never obeyed—this is how the quarrel arose.'
translations.idiomatic: and they were forced to sign a pledge that any renewed smuggling would mean confiscation and immediate execution, which they never accepted. That is how the trouble began.'

sentences.zh: 當義律具禀繳煙，距撤退買辦五日，非出情原。

translations.literal: When Elliot submitted his memorial surrendering opium, it was only five days after the compradors had been withdrawn—not an act of willing submission.
translations.idiomatic: When Elliot formally surrendered the opium, it was only five days after the compradors had been sent away—not a gesture made willingly.

sentences.zh: 時義律僅止孤身，設有黨援，未必降心俯首。

translations.literal: At that time Elliot was alone; had he had supporters at hand, he might not have bowed his head so readily.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Elliot stood alone; with allies behind him he might not have submitted so meekly.

sentences.zh: 英吉利國王無給林則徐文書之事，惟呂宋國王曾有來文，或因此誤傳。

translations.literal: The King of England never sent Lin Zexu any document; only the King of Luzon had once written, and the story may have arisen from that confusion.
translations.idiomatic: The King of England never wrote to Lin Zexu; only the King of Luzon had sent a letter, and the report may have confused the two.

sentences.zh: 林則徐稱定海陰濕，洋人病死甚多。

translations.literal: Lin Zexu claimed that Dinghai was damp and gloomy and that many foreigners had died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zexu claimed that Dinghai's damp climate had killed many foreigners.

sentences.zh: 諮查洋人米穀牲畜尚充，疫癘病斃者多水手舵工，頭目死者不過數人。

translations.literal: On inquiry, the foreigners still had ample grain, livestock, and provisions; most who died of epidemic were sailors and helmsmen, and only a few officers had perished.
translations.idiomatic: Inquiry showed their stores of grain and livestock were still ample. Most epidemic deaths were among sailors and helmsmen; only a handful of officers had died.

sentences.zh: 從前外洋來信，祗言貿易。

translations.literal: Former letters from overseas spoke only of trade.
translations.idiomatic: Past letters from abroad had spoken only of trade.

sentences.zh: 自林則徐欲悉外情，多方購求漁利之人，造作播傳，真偽互見，此時紛紛查探，適墮術中。

translations.literal: Since Lin Zexu wished to learn all foreign circumstances, he bought information widely from profiteers, who fabricated and spread reports so that truth and falsehood mingled; at this time investigations were launched on every side and fell straight into their trap.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lin Zexu set out to learn everything about the foreigners, he paid widely for tips from opportunists who invented and circulated stories, mixing truth with fiction. The flurry of investigations at this time played straight into their hands.

sentences.zh: 林則徐奏各國憤英人阻其貿易，美利堅、法蘭西將遣船來與理論。

translations.literal: Lin Zexu memorialized that every nation resented the English for blocking their trade, and that the United States and France would send ships to reason with them.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zexu reported that other countries were angry at Britain for blocking their trade and that the United States and France would send warships to settle accounts with the English.

sentences.zh: 訪聞各國曾有此說，然迄未見兵船來粵。

translations.literal: On inquiry, such talk had indeed been heard among the nations, but no warships had yet come to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Inquiry showed such talk had circulated, yet no foreign warships had actually appeared in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 前有美國二船，乘英人不備，進口，至今未敢駛出。

translations.literal: Earlier two American ships had entered port while the English were off guard, and to this day they have not dared to sail out.
translations.idiomatic: Two American vessels had earlier slipped into port while the British were unprepared, and they still had not dared to leave.

sentences.zh: 畏葸如斯，縱力足頡頏，恐未肯傷其同類。

translations.literal: So timid were they that even if strong enough to contend, they would probably not harm their own kind.
translations.idiomatic: So timid were they that even with strength enough to stand up to Britain, they would hardly strike their own kind.

sentences.zh: 虎門燒煙時，洋人觀者撰文數千言紀事，事誠有之，語多含譏刺，非心服。

translations.literal: At the burning of opium at Humen, foreign onlookers wrote accounts of several thousand words; the event indeed occurred, but the language was largely sarcastic and showed no heartfelt submission.
translations.idiomatic: When opium was burned at Humen, foreign spectators wrote lengthy accounts of the event. The incident was real enough, but their tone was largely sarcastic—they were not won over in spirit.

sentences.zh: 林則徐稱具結之後，查驗他國來船，絕無鴉片。

translations.literal: Lin Zexu claimed that after the pledges were submitted, inspection of ships from other countries found no opium at all.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zexu claimed that after the pledges were signed, inspections of other nations' ships found no opium whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 如指上年而言，事屬以往，船貨無憑；

translations.literal: If he meant the previous year, that belongs to the past and there is no proof from ships or cargo;
translations.idiomatic: If he meant the previous year, that was already past and there is no way to verify ships or cargo;

sentences.zh: 若指本年而言，來船尚未進口，不能知其有，亦安能信其無？

translations.literal: if he meant this year, the incoming ships have not yet entered port—how can one know they have it, and how can one believe they do not?'
translations.idiomatic: if he meant this year, the incoming ships have not yet docked—how can one know they carry opium, and how can one be sure they do not?'

sentences.zh: 」並言將軍阿精阿請團練水勇，及林則徐請鼓勵員弁，俟事定再議。

translations.literal: ' He also said that General Ajing'a had requested militia training for naval braves, and that Lin Zexu's request to reward officers and men should wait until affairs were settled.
translations.idiomatic: ' He added that General Ajing'a had asked to organize militia river forces, and that Lin Zexu's proposal to reward officers and men should be deferred until the crisis was resolved.

sentences.zh: 疏入，報聞，則徐以是獲罪。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, acknowledgment was returned; Lin Zexu was punished on this account.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received and noted; Lin Zexu was condemned on its basis.

sentences.zh: 時廣東撤水師歸營，猝被敵轟擊，掠去米艇兵丁，巡撫怡良以聞。

translations.literal: At that time Guangdong had withdrawn the naval force to barracks; they were suddenly bombarded by the enemy, who seized grain boats and soldiers; Governor Yiliang reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong had just withdrawn its naval force to barracks when the enemy suddenly opened fire, seized grain boats and troops, and Governor Yiliang reported the attack.

sentences.zh: 琦善又陳：「英人回粵，詞氣傲慢，義律託疾將回國，且兵船日增。

translations.literal: Qi Shan further reported: 'The English returned to Guangdong with arrogant language; Elliot pleaded illness and said he would return home, while warships increased daily.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan reported again: 'The English returned to Guangdong speaking arrogantly. Elliot claimed illness and said he would go home, while warships were arriving daily.

sentences.zh: 」得旨，仍暫停貿易，一面與議，一面籌防。

translations.literal: ' An edict was received: trade was still to be suspended for the time being, while negotiations proceeded on one side and defenses were prepared on the other.
translations.idiomatic: ' The court ordered trade to remain suspended for now while talks continued on one hand and defenses were readied on the other.

sentences.zh: 義律堅持索還煙價，並增廈門、福州通商，嚴旨拒不許。

translations.literal: Elliot insisted on repayment for the destroyed opium and on opening trade at Xiamen and Fuzhou as well; stern edicts refused permission.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot insisted on compensation for the destroyed opium and on opening Xiamen and Fuzhou to trade as well, but stern edicts refused both demands.

sentences.zh: 十二月，義律見防禦漸撤，數遣挑戰，琦善諭止之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Elliot saw defenses being gradually withdrawn and repeatedly sent challenges; Qi Shan instructed him to stop.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Elliot noticed defenses thinning and sent repeated provocations; Qi Shan ordered him to desist.

sentences.zh: 義律曰：「戰後再議，未為遲也。

translations.literal: Elliot said: 'To negotiate after fighting would not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot replied: 'We can talk after we fight—it will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 」乃犯虎門外沙角、大角兩砲台，副將陳連升力戰死之，遂陷。

translations.literal: ' He then attacked the Shajiao and Dajiao batteries outside Humen; Vice Commander Chen Liansheng fought fiercely and died, and the forts fell.
translations.idiomatic: ' He then assaulted the Shajiao and Dajiao batteries outside Humen. Vice Commander Chen Liansheng fought to the death, and both forts were taken.

sentences.zh: 提督關天培守靖遠砲台，總兵李廷鈺守威遠砲台，並請援，琦善不敢明發兵，夜遣二百人往。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Guan Tianpei held Jingyuan battery and Brigadier Li Tingyu held Weiyuan battery; both asked for reinforcements. Qi Shan dared not dispatch troops openly and sent two hundred men by night.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Guan Tianpei held Jingyuan battery and Brigadier Li Tingyu held Weiyuan; both begged for help. Qi Shan would not send troops openly and sent only two hundred men by night.

sentences.zh: 二十一年正月，事聞，上震怒，下琦善嚴議，命御前大臣貝子奕山為靖逆將軍，戶部尚書隆文、湖南提督楊芳副之，率師赴粵協剿。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-first year, when the matter was reported, the emperor was greatly angered, placed Qi Shan under severe investigation, appointed the imperial clansman Prince Yishan as Pacification Commissioner, with Minister Long Wen of the Ministry of Revenue and Hunan Regional Commander Yang Fang as deputies, to lead troops to Guangdong for joint suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When news reached court in the first month of Daoguang 21 (1841), the emperor was furious. Qi Shan was placed under severe investigation. Prince Yishan was named Pacification Commissioner, with Minister Long Wen and Hunan Regional Commander Yang Fang as deputies, to lead an army to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 義律數索香港，志在必得，琦善當事急，佯許之而不敢上聞。

translations.literal: Elliot repeatedly demanded Hong Kong, determined to obtain it; Qi Shan, pressed by the emergency, pretended to agree but did not dare report it.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot repeatedly demanded Hong Kong and meant to have it. Under pressure, Qi Shan pretended to agree but never reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 至是，義律獻出所踞砲台，並原繳還定海以易香港全島，別議通商章程。

translations.literal: At this point Elliot offered the batteries he held and proposed to return Dinghai in exchange for the whole island of Hong Kong, with trade regulations to be discussed separately.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot then offered to hand back the batteries he held and to restore Dinghai in exchange for the whole of Hong Kong, with trade terms to be negotiated separately.

sentences.zh: 琦善親與相見蓮花城定議，往返傳語，由差遣之鮑鵬將事，同城將軍、巡撫皆不預知。

translations.literal: Qi Shan met him in person at Lianhuacheng to settle terms, exchanging messages back and forth; the envoy Bao Peng handled affairs, while the general and governor in the same city were not informed beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan met Elliot in person at Lianhuacheng to settle terms, messages passing back and forth through the envoy Bao Peng. The regional commander and governor in the same city knew nothing in advance.

sentences.zh: 及英人佔踞香港，出示安民，巡撫怡良奏聞，琦善方疏陳：「地勢無可扼，軍械無可恃，兵力不固，民情不堅，如與交鋒，實無把握，不如暫事羈縻。

translations.literal: When the English occupied Hong Kong and issued a proclamation to reassure the people, Governor Yiliang memorialized the throne; only then did Qi Shan report: 'The terrain offers no choke point, arms are unreliable, troops are not solid, and popular sentiment is not firm; if we engage, we truly have no assurance—better to temporize for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: After the British seized Hong Kong and issued a placard to calm the populace, Governor Yiliang reported to the throne. Only then did Qi Shan write: 'The ground cannot be held, weapons cannot be trusted, troops are unreliable, and the people are not steadfast. We have no real chance in a fight—it is better to temporize.

sentences.zh: 」上益怒，詔斥琦善擅予香港，擅許通商之罪，褫職逮治，籍沒家產。

translations.literal: ' The emperor grew still angrier. An edict rebuked Qi Shan for giving away Hong Kong on his own authority and for permitting trade on his own authority; he was stripped of office, arrested, and his property confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor's rage deepened. An edict condemned Qi Shan for ceding Hong Kong and allowing trade on his own authority, stripped him of office, ordered his arrest, and confiscated his property.

sentences.zh: 英兵遂奪虎門靖遠砲台，提督關天培死之。

translations.literal: The British then seized the Jingyuan battery at Humen, and Regional Commander Guan Tianpei died.
translations.idiomatic: British forces then took the Jingyuan battery at Humen, and Regional Commander Guan Tianpei was killed.

sentences.zh: 奕山等至，戰復不利，廣州危急，許以煙價六百萬兩，圍始解，而福建、浙江復被擾。

translations.literal: When Yishan and the others arrived, fighting went badly again; Guangzhou was in peril; six million taels were promised for the opium indemnity before the siege was lifted, while Fujian and Zhejiang were harassed anew.
translations.idiomatic: Yishan's force arrived but fighting went badly again. Guangzhou was in peril. Six million taels were promised as opium indemnity before the siege lifted, while Fujian and Zhejiang were raided again.

sentences.zh: 琦善逮京，讞論大辟，尋釋之，命赴浙江軍營效力，未至，改發軍台。

translations.literal: Qi Shan was brought to the capital; judgment called for capital punishment, but he was soon released and ordered to serve at the Zhejiang army camp; before he arrived he was instead sent to a military post.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan was taken to the capital. Sentence called for death, but he was soon released and ordered to serve in the Zhejiang army. Before he arrived, he was reassigned to a frontier military post instead.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，浙師复敗，吳淞不守，英兵遂入江，江寧戒嚴，於是耆英、伊里布等定和議，海內莫不以罷戰言和歸咎於琦善為作俑之始矣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the Zhejiang army was defeated again, Wusong could not be held, and British troops entered the Yangtze; Jiangning was placed under martial law. Thereupon Qiying, Yi Libu, and others settled a peace, and throughout the realm the decision to cease fighting and sue for peace was blamed on Qi Shan as the one who had started it.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 22 (1842) the Zhejiang force was beaten again, Wusong fell, and British troops pushed up the Yangtze until Jiangning was placed under martial law. Qiying, Yi Libu, and others then negotiated peace, and across the empire the turn to truce was blamed on Qi Shan as the man who had set it in motion.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，予四等侍衛，充葉爾羌幫辦大臣。

translations.literal: That autumn he was given the rank of fourth-class bodyguard and appointed assistant commissioner at Yarkand.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was made a fourth-class imperial guardsman and appointed assistant commissioner at Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以三品頂戴授熱河都統。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, with third-rank insignia, he was appointed military governor of Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 23 (1843) he received third-rank insignia and was appointed military governor of Rehe.

sentences.zh: 御史陳慶鏞疏論僨事諸臣罪狀，上重違清議，再褫琦善職，意仍鄉用，未幾，予三等侍衛，充駐藏大臣。

translations.literal: Censor Chen Qingyong memorialized on the crimes of the officials involved in the war; the emperor, weighing pure opinion heavily, again stripped Qi Shan of office, though he still intended to employ him locally. Before long Qi Shan was given third-class bodyguard rank and appointed resident commissioner in Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Qingyong listed the faults of the war ministers. The emperor, mindful of public opinion, stripped Qi Shan of office again, though he still meant to use him. Soon Qi Shan was made a third-class guardsman and appointed resident commissioner in Tibet.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授四川總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Sichuan governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 26 (1846) he was appointed governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，詔嘉其治蜀於吏治營伍實心整頓，复頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year an edict praised his governance of Shu for earnestly reforming civil administration and the army, and his first-rank insignia was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 28 (1848) an edict praised his earnest reform of civil administration and the army in Sichuan, and his first-rank insignia was restored.

sentences.zh: 尋協辦大學士，留總督任。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he became an associate grand secretary while retaining the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made associate grand secretary while keeping his post as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 以平瞻對野番功被議敘。

translations.literal: For pacifying the Zhanduiye barbarians he received a merit citation.
translations.idiomatic: He earned a merit citation for pacifying the Zhanduiye tribes.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，調陝甘總督，兼署青海辦事大臣，剿雍沙番及黑城撒拉回匪。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general, also acting as Qinghai commissioner, and suppressed the Yongsha tribes and the Salar rebels at Heicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 29 (1849) he was transferred to governor-general of Shaanxi-Gansu and acted as Qinghai commissioner, campaigning against the Yongsha tribes and the Salar rebels at Heicheng.

sentences.zh: 既而言官劾其妄殺，命都統薩迎阿往按，革職逮問。

translations.literal: Soon censors impeached him for indiscriminate killing; Commander-in-chief Saying'a was sent to investigate; he was dismissed and arrested for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Censors soon accused him of reckless killing. Commander-in-chief Saying'a was sent to investigate, and Qi Shan was dismissed and arrested.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，定讞發吉林效力贖罪，尋釋回。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng judgment was fixed: he was sent to Jilin to redeem his crime through service, and was soon released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 2 (1852) he was sentenced to serve in Jilin to redeem his crime and was soon released.

sentences.zh: 時粵匪已犯湖南，勢日熾，屢易帥皆不能制。

translations.literal: At that time the Guangdong rebels had already invaded Hunan; their power grew daily, and repeated changes of commander could not contain them.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiping rebels had already entered Hunan, their strength growing daily, and repeated command changes had failed to stop them.

sentences.zh: 起琦善署河南巡撫，駐防楚、豫界上。

translations.literal: Qi Shan was recalled to act as Henan governor and stationed on the Hubei-Henan border for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan was recalled to serve as acting governor of Henan and posted on the Hubei-Henan frontier.

sentences.zh: 以捐餉加都統銜，授欽差大臣，專辦防務。

translations.literal: For contributing funds he was given commander-in-chief rank and appointed imperial commissioner solely to handle defense.
translations.idiomatic: For donating supplies he received commander-in-chief rank and was named imperial commissioner in charge of defense.

sentences.zh: 湖北省城失守，觀望不能救。

translations.literal: When the Hubei provincial capital fell, he looked on and could not save it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hubei provincial capital fell, he held back and failed to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 三年春，賊遂連陷安徽、江寧省城，分擾鎮江、揚州，命琦善偕直隸提督陳金​​綬防江北。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year the rebels in succession took the Anhui and Jiangning provincial capitals and raided Zhenjiang and Yangzhou in detachments; Qi Shan was ordered, together with Zhili Regional Commander Chen Jinshou, to defend the north bank of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Xianfeng 3 (1853) the rebels took the Anhui and Jiangning capitals in turn and raided Zhenjiang and Yangzhou. Qi Shan was ordered, with Zhili Regional Commander Chen Jinshou, to defend the north bank of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 三月，連敗賊於浦口雷塘，進剿揚州，分屯寶塔山、司徒廟，五戰皆捷。

translations.literal: In the third month he repeatedly defeated the rebels at Pukou and Leitang, advanced to suppress Yangzhou, and encamped separately at Baota Hill and Situgong Temple; five battles were all victorious.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he beat the rebels repeatedly at Pukou and Leitang, advanced on Yangzhou, and encamped at Baota Hill and Situgong Temple. Five engagements all ended in victory.

sentences.zh: 秋，破浦口援賊，合圍揚州。

translations.literal: In autumn he broke the rebel relief force at Pukou and jointly besieged Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he routed rebel reinforcements at Pukou and joined the siege of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，賊突圍出竄瓜洲，以收復揚州入告，詔斥勇潰縱賊，責令進剿瓜洲、儀徵，儀徵克復。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the rebels broke out of the encirclement and fled to Guazhou; he reported the recovery of Yangzhou, but an edict rebuked the troops for cowardice and letting the enemy escape, and ordered him to advance against Guazhou and Yizheng; Yizheng was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the rebels broke out and fled to Guazhou. He reported Yangzhou as recovered, but an edict rebuked his troops for cowardice and letting the enemy escape, and ordered him to advance on Guazhou and Yizheng. Yizheng was retaken.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，連戰金川、瓜洲、三汊河，屢奏斬獲。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year he fought repeatedly at Jinchuan, Guazhou, and San Cha River, and repeatedly reported kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Xianfeng 4 (1854) he fought repeatedly at Jinchuan, Guazhou, and San Cha River and repeatedly reported enemy killed and captured.

sentences.zh: 自琦善與向榮分主大江南北軍事，攻戰年餘，鎮江、瓜洲迄未克復，無得力水師，不能扼賊，琦善雖議增水師，亦未果。

translations.literal: From the time Qi Shan and Xiang Rong divided command of military affairs north and south of the Yangtze, they fought for more than a year, yet Zhenjiang and Guazhou were never recovered; without an effective naval force they could not choke the rebels, and though Qi Shan proposed expanding the navy, it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi Shan and Xiang Rong divided command north and south of the Yangtze, they fought for more than a year without retaking Zhenjiang or Guazhou. Lacking a capable navy they could not block the rebels. Qi Shan proposed building up the fleet, but nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，卒於軍，贈太子太保、協辦大學士，依總督例賜卹，諡文勤。

translations.literal: That autumn he died in camp. He was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and associate grand secretary, mourning grants according to the governor-general precedent, and the posthumous title Wenqin.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he died in camp. He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and associate grand secretary, granted mourning benefits as for a governor-general, and given the posthumous name Wenqin (Diligent in Culture).

sentences.zh: 恭鏜 子恭鏜，黑龍江將軍。

translations.literal: Gongqin. His son Gongqin was military governor of Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Gongqin. His son Gongqin served as military governor of Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 孫瑞洵，烏里雅蘇台參贊大臣；

translations.literal: His grandson Ruixun was commissioner at Uliastai;
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Ruixun was commissioner at Uliastai;

sentences.zh: 瑞澂，兩湖總督。

translations.literal: Ruicheng was governor-general of the Two Hubeis.
translations.idiomatic: Ruicheng was governor-general of the Two Hubeis.

sentences.zh: 瑞澂自有傳。

translations.literal: Ruicheng has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Ruicheng has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 伊里布 伊里布，字莘農，鑲黃旗紅帶子。

translations.literal: Yi Libu. Yi Libu, style name Xinnong, was a bondsman of the Bordered Yellow Banner with red girdle.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Libu. Yi Libu, whose style was Xinnong, was a bondsman of the Bordered Yellow Banner entitled to wear the red girdle.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年進士，授國子監學正，改補典簿。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the sixth year of Jiaqing, he was appointed director of studies at the Imperial Academy and later transferred to archivist.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Jiaqing 6 (1801), became director of studies at the Imperial Academy, and was later transferred to archivist.

sentences.zh: 出為雲南府南關通判，署澂江知府，遷騰越知州。

translations.literal: He went out as subprefect of Nanguan in Yunnan Prefecture, acted as prefect of Chengjiang, and was transferred to magistrate of Tengyue.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as subprefect of Nanguan in Yunnan Prefecture, acted as prefect of Chengjiang, and was promoted to magistrate of Tengyue.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，總督伯麟薦其熟練邊務，能馭土司，治緬匪有功，以應升用。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Governor Bailing recommended him as skilled in frontier affairs, able to control native chiefs, and meritorious in suppressing Burmese bandits, deserving promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 24 (1819) Governor Bailing recommended him as skilled in frontier affairs, able to manage native chiefs, and successful against Burmese raiders, deserving promotion.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，從總督慶保剿平永北大姚夷匪，賜花翎，署永昌知府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang, following Governor Qingbao, he suppressed the Yi rebels of Yongbei and Dayao, was granted the peacock feather, and acted as prefect of Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 1 (1821), serving under Governor Qingbao, he put down the Yi rebels of Yongbei and Dayao, received the peacock feather, and acted as prefect of Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 擢安徽太平知府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to prefect of Taiping in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Taiping in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 歷山西冀寧道，浙江按察使，湖北、浙江布政使。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Jining circuit intendant in Shanxi, Zhejiang surveillance commissioner, and Hubei and Zhejiang provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Jining circuit intendant in Shanxi, surveillance commissioner of Zhejiang, and provincial treasurer of Hubei and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢陝西巡撫，調山東。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Shaanxi governor and transferred to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 5 (1825) he was promoted to governor of Shaanxi and transferred to Shandong.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，署雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: When his father died he was released from mourning to act as Yunnan governor.
translations.idiomatic: On his father's death he was recalled from mourning to act as governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 服闋，乃實授。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he received formal appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended he received the post in full.

sentences.zh: 時阮元為總督，伊里布和而廉，有政聲。

translations.literal: At that time Ruan Yuan was governor-general; Yi Libu was mild and incorrupt, and enjoyed a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Yuan was then governor-general. Yi Libu was mild and upright and enjoyed a strong reputation for governance.

sentences.zh: 回疆兵事起，自請從軍，詔斥不諳回情，妄行陳奏，奪職留任，尋復之。

translations.literal: When military affairs arose in the Western Regions he volunteered for the campaign; an edict rebuked him for not understanding the situation there and for rash memorializing; he was stripped of office but kept in his post, and soon restored.
translations.idiomatic: When fighting broke out in the Western Regions he volunteered for service. The throne rebuked him for not understanding frontier conditions and for rash memorializing, stripped him of rank but kept him in post, and soon restored him.

sentences.zh: 十三年，擢雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 13 he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 京察，以久任邊疆，鎮撫得宜，被議敘。

translations.literal: At the capital inspection, for long service on the frontier and proper pacification, he received a merit citation.
translations.idiomatic: At the metropolitan review he earned a merit citation for long frontier service and effective pacification.

sentences.zh: 十八年，協辦大學士，留總督任。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he became an associate grand secretary while retaining the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 18 he was made associate grand secretary while keeping his post as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 四川綦江奸民穆繼賢仇殺貴州仁懷武生趙應彩，遂糾眾踞方家溝為亂，伊里布率提督余步雲、布政使慶祿等破其巢，斬獲千餘，誅賊首穆繼賢、謝法真等，餘匪悉平，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: A villain of Qijiang in Sichuan, Mu Jixian, killed in revenge the military licentiate Zhao Yingcai of Renhuai in Guizhou, then gathered a crowd and seized Fangjiagou in rebellion. Yi Libu led Regional Commander Yu Buyun, Provincial Treasurer Qinglu, and others to destroy their lair; more than a thousand were killed or captured; the rebel leaders Mu Jixian, Xie Fazhen, and others were executed; the rest were all pacified; he was granted the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Jixian, a ruffian of Qijiang in Sichuan, killed Zhao Yingcai, a military licentiate of Renhuai in Guizhou, in a feud, then rallied followers and seized Fangjiagou in revolt. Yi Libu led Regional Commander Yu Buyun, Provincial Treasurer Qinglu, and others to smash their stronghold, killing or capturing more than a thousand and executing the leaders Mu Jixian and Xie Fazhen. The remaining bandits were pacified, and he received the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 十九年，調兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was transferred to the Two Jiangs governor-generalship.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 19 he was transferred to governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 二十年秋，英兵陷定海，命為欽差大臣，赴浙江查辦。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twentieth year the English took Dinghai; he was appointed imperial commissioner and sent to Zhejiang to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Daoguang 20 the British seized Dinghai. He was named imperial commissioner and sent to investigate in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 時已有論致寇由斷絕貿易燒煙起釁者，密諭察訪確情毋回護。

translations.literal: There were already those who argued that the enemy had been provoked by cutting off trade and burning opium; he was secretly instructed to investigate the true facts and not cover up.
translations.idiomatic: Some already argued that the enemy had been provoked by cutting off trade and burning opium. He was secretly told to investigate the facts and not shield anyone.

sentences.zh: 尋以琦善代林則徐，命沿海遇敵勿擊。

translations.literal: Soon Qi Shan replaced Lin Zexu, and coastal officials were ordered not to attack when they met the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan soon replaced Lin Zexu, and coastal officials were ordered not to fire on the enemy.

sentences.zh: 伊里布初至浙，駐鎮海籌防，疏報擊沉敵船，有所擒獲，命慰諭英人攻擊出於誤會，促令退兵交地，俘虜俟敵退釋還。

translations.literal: When Yi Libu first reached Zhejiang he stationed himself at Zhenhai to organize defense, memorialized that he had sunk enemy ships and taken captives, and was ordered to reassure the English that the attack arose from misunderstanding, urge them to withdraw and return territory, and release prisoners after the enemy retreated.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Zhejiang Yi Libu based himself at Zhenhai to organize defenses and reported sinking enemy ships and taking prisoners. He was told to assure the British the clash was a misunderstanding, urge withdrawal and return of occupied ground, and release prisoners once they left.

sentences.zh: 伊里布遣家丁張喜偕員弁赴定海犒師，英人亦答餽，奏聞，諭卻勿受。

translations.literal: Yi Libu sent his household servant Zhang Xi with officers to Dinghai to reward the troops; the English also returned gifts; he reported this, and was instructed to refuse them.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Libu sent his servant Zhang Xi with officers to Dinghai to present gifts to the troops. The British sent gifts in return. When he reported this, the court ordered him to refuse them.

sentences.zh: 請增調安徽、兩湖兵，允之。

translations.literal: He requested additional troops from Anhui and the Two Hubeis; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for reinforcements from Anhui and the Two Hubeis, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 裕謙方代署兩江總督，疏言：「各省皆可議守，獨浙江必應速戰。

translations.literal: Yu Qian had just acted as Two Jiangs governor-general and memorialized: 'Every province may discuss defense, but Zhejiang alone must fight quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian, then acting governor-general of the Two Jiangs, wrote: 'Every province may talk of holding defensive positions, but Zhejiang must fight at once.

sentences.zh: 」且言：「定海西境岑港為第一險要，應以精兵先據之。

translations.literal: ' He also said: 'Cengang on the western border of Dinghai is the foremost strategic point and should be seized first by elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: ' He added: 'Cengang on Dinghai's western flank is the key point and should be seized first by picked troops.

sentences.zh: 」下伊里布體察辦理。

translations.literal: ' The matter was referred to Yi Libu for investigation and action.
translations.idiomatic: ' The order went to Yi Libu to investigate and act accordingly.

sentences.zh: 既而琦善在粵議款不得要領，兵端又開，二十一年正月，詔促伊里布進兵規复定海。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Qi Shan's peace talks in Guangdong failed to gain the essentials and fighting reopened; in the first month of the twenty-first year an edict urged Yi Libu to advance and recover Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shan's peace talks in Guangdong then broke down and fighting resumed. In the first month of Daoguang 21 an edict pressed Yi Libu to advance and retake Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 二月，義律既踞香港，盡調英船赴粵，以交還定海告。

translations.literal: In the second month Elliot, having seized Hong Kong, transferred all British ships to Guangdong and announced he would return Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Elliot, having taken Hong Kong, moved all British ships to Guangdong and offered to return Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 詔斥附和琦善，以兵砲未集，藉詞緩攻，致敵船遁去，褫協辦大學士、雙眼花翎，暫留兩江總督任，以裕謙代為欽差大臣督浙師。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked him for siding with Qi Shan, citing the excuse that troops and guns were not yet assembled to delay the attack and letting the enemy ships escape; he was stripped of associate grand secretary rank and the double-eyed peacock feather, temporarily kept as Two Jiangs governor-general, and Yu Qian replaced him as imperial commissioner commanding the Zhejiang army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict condemned him for echoing Qi Shan, claiming troops and artillery were not ready as a pretext to delay attack while the enemy escaped. He lost his associate grand secretary rank and double-eyed peacock feather, kept the Two Jiangs post for the moment, and Yu Qian replaced him as imperial commissioner over the Zhejiang forces.

sentences.zh: 裕謙論劾伊里布遣家丁赴敵船事，命解任，帶張喜來京，下刑部訊鞫，褫職，遣戍軍台。

translations.literal: Yu Qian impeached Yi Libu for sending his servant to the enemy ships; he was ordered dismissed, Zhang Xi was brought to the capital, the Ministry of Punishments interrogated him, his office was stripped, and he was banished to a military post.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian impeached Yi Libu for sending his servant to enemy ships. He was dismissed, Zhang Xi was brought to the capital, the Ministry of Punishments tried the case, Yi Libu was stripped of office, and banished to a frontier post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，定海、鎮海、寧波相繼陷，裕謙殉之。

translations.literal: Before long Dinghai, Zhenhai, and Ningbo fell in succession, and Yu Qian died for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Dinghai, Zhenhai, and Ningbo fell in turn, and Yu Qian died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 二十二年春，揚威將軍奕經援浙，復挫敗。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-second year the Pacification General Yijing reinforced Zhejiang but was defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Daoguang 22 Pacification General Yijing reinforced Zhejiang but was beaten again.

sentences.zh: 巡撫劉韻珂疏陳浙事危急，薦伊里布無急功近名之心，為一時僅見，請發軍營效力贖罪。

translations.literal: Governor Liu Yunke memorialized that Zhejiang affairs were critical, recommended Yi Libu as free of eagerness for quick success or fame—a rare man of the time—and asked that he be sent to army camp to redeem his crime through service.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Liu Yunke reported that Zhejiang was in crisis and recommended Yi Libu as a rare official without hunger for quick glory, asking that he be sent to the army to redeem his crime through service.

sentences.zh: 於是予七品頂戴，隨杭州將軍耆英赴浙，密諭相機辦理。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was given seventh-rank insignia and followed Hangzhou General Qiying to Zhejiang, with secret instructions to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: He was then given seventh-rank insignia and accompanied Hangzhou General Qiying to Zhejiang with secret orders to act as circumstances allowed.

sentences.zh: 及英兵犯乍浦，耆英遣往設計退兵。

translations.literal: When the English attacked Zhapu, Qiying sent him to devise means to make them withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When the British attacked Zhapu, Qiying sent him to arrange their withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 五月，署乍浦副都統，復令張喜傳語，英兵遂去乍浦，犯吳淞，由海入江，鎮江失守。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he acted as Zhapu deputy commander-in-chief and again had Zhang Xi convey messages; the English then left Zhapu, attacked Wusong, entered the Yangtze from the sea, and Zhenjiang fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he acted as deputy commander at Zhapu and again used Zhang Xi as envoy. The British left Zhapu, attacked Wusong, entered the Yangtze from the sea, and Zhenjiang fell.

sentences.zh: 伊里布奉命偕耆英赴江寧議和，事詳耆英傳。

translations.literal: Yi Libu was ordered to join Qiying at Jiangning to negotiate peace; the details are given in Qiying's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Libu was ordered to join Qiying at Jiangning to negotiate peace, as recounted in Qiying's biography.

sentences.zh: 和議既成，英兵退，約於廣東議稅則，命偕耆英詳慎酌商，授廣州將軍、欽差大臣，辦理善後事宜。

translations.literal: Once peace was settled and the English withdrew, it was agreed to discuss tariff regulations in Guangdong; he was ordered to join Qiying in careful consultation, appointed Guangzhou general and imperial commissioner, and charged with postwar arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was made and the British withdrew, tariff talks were set for Guangdong. He was ordered to consult carefully with Qiying, appointed Guangzhou general and imperial commissioner, and put in charge of postwar arrangements.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，至粵，見民心不服，夷情狡橫，憂悴。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he reached Guangdong, saw popular discontent, found the foreigners crafty and overbearing, and was worn with worry.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 23 he reached Guangdong, found the people resentful and the foreigners arrogant and treacherous, and was consumed with anxiety.

sentences.zh: 踰月病卒，贈太子太保，諡文敏。

translations.literal: After more than a month he died of illness. He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later he died of illness. He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Wenmin (Acute in Culture).

sentences.zh: 宗室耆英 宗室耆英，字介春，隸正藍旗。

translations.literal: Imperial clansman Qiying. Qiying, style name Jiechun, belonged to the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansman Qiying. Qiying, whose style was Jiechun, came from the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 父祿康，嘉慶間官東閣大學士。

translations.literal: His father Lukang served as Grand Secretary of the Dongge Pavilion during the Jiaqing reign.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lukang served as Grand Secretary of the Dongge Pavilion under Jiaqing.

sentences.zh: 耆英以廕生授宗人府主事，遷理事官。

translations.literal: Qiying entered through the yin privilege as a director in the Imperial Clan Court and was promoted to supervising director.
translations.idiomatic: Qiying entered through hereditary privilege as a director in the Imperial Clan Court and rose to supervising director.

sentences.zh: 累擢內閣學士，兼副都統、護軍統​​領。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to Grand Secretariat academician, and concurrently served as deputy commander-in-chief and commandant of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Grand Secretariat academician and concurrently served as deputy commander-in-chief and guards commandant.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，遷理籓院侍郎，調兵部。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he was transferred to vice president of the Court of Colonial Affairs and then to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 2 he moved to vice president of the Court of Colonial Affairs and then to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 四年，送宗室閒散移駐雙城堡。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he escorted idle imperial clansmen to resettle at Shuangcheng Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 4 he escorted idle imperial clansmen to resettle at Shuangcheng Fort.

sentences.zh: 五年，授內務府大臣，歷工部、戶部。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed minister of the Imperial Household Department and served in the Ministries of Works and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 5 he became minister of the Imperial Household Department and later served in the Ministries of Works and Revenue.

sentences.zh: 七年，授步軍統領。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed commandant of the Metropolitan Gendarmerie.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 7 he was appointed commandant of the Metropolitan Gendarmerie.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢禮部尚書，管理太常寺、鴻​​臚寺、太醫院，兼都統。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to Minister of Rites, placed in charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, the Court of Ceremonies, and the Imperial Medical Institute, and also served as commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 9 he was promoted to Minister of Rites, placed over the sacrificial, ceremonial, and medical offices, and also served as commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十二年，畿輔旱，疏請察吏省刑，嘉納之，授內大臣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, when the capital region suffered drought, he memorialized requesting scrutiny of officials and reduction of punishments; this was well received and he was made a grand minister of the interior.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 12 drought struck the capital region. He asked for tighter scrutiny of officials and lighter punishments. The throne approved and made him a grand minister of the interior.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以管理步軍統領勤事，被議敘。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, for diligent service as commandant of the Metropolitan Gendarmerie, he received a merit citation.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 14 he earned a merit citation for diligent management of the Metropolitan Gendarmerie.

sentences.zh: 歷工部、戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Minister of Works and Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Minister of Works and Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以相度龍泉峪萬年吉地，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, for surveying the auspicious tomb site at Longquanyu, he was given Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 15, for surveying the imperial tomb site at Longquanyu, he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 命赴廣東、江西按事。

translations.literal: He was ordered to investigate affairs in Guangdong and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to investigate affairs in Guangdong and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 十七年，內監張道忠犯賭博，耆英瞻徇釋放，事覺，降兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the eunuch Zhang Daozhong was guilty of gambling; Qiying showed favoritism and released him; when the matter came to light he was demoted to vice president of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 17 the eunuch Zhang Daozhong was caught gambling. Qiying favored him and ordered his release. When the affair surfaced, Qiying was demoted to vice president of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 尋出為熱河都統。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he went out as military governor of Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted as military governor of Rehe.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授盛京將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed general of Shengjing.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 18 he was appointed general of Shengjing.

sentences.zh: 詔嚴禁鴉片，無論宗室、覺羅，按律懲治。

translations.literal: An edict strictly forbade opium; whether imperial clansmen or gioro, all were to be punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: An edict strictly banned opium and required imperial clansmen and gioro alike to be punished under the law.

sentences.zh: 疏請旗民十家聯保，以憑稽察。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting mutual guarantee groups of ten banner households for inspection purposes.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that banner households be grouped in tens for mutual guarantee to aid inspection.

sentences.zh: 二十年，海疆戒嚴，疏請旅順口為水路衝衢，當扼要籌備。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the maritime frontier was placed under martial law; he memorialized that Lüshunkou was a key water route and should be held by strategic preparation.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 20 the coast was placed under martial law. He reported that Lüshunkou was a vital water route and must be fortified.

sentences.zh: 英船入奉天洋面，先後游弋山海關、秦皇島等處，錦州、山海關皆設防。

translations.literal: British ships entered the Fengtian sea area and successively cruised off Shanhaiguan, Qinhuangdao, and other places; defenses were set at Jinzhou and Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: British ships entered Fengtian waters and cruised off Shanhaiguan, Qinhuangdao, and other points. Defenses were raised at Jinzhou and Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 二十二年正月，粵事急，琦善既黜，調耆英廣州將軍，授欽差大臣，督辦浙江洋務。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-second year Guangdong affairs grew urgent; Qi Shan had already been dismissed; Qiying was transferred to Guangzhou general, appointed imperial commissioner, and put in charge of Zhejiang maritime affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Daoguang 22, with Guangdong in crisis and Qi Shan dismissed, Qiying was made Guangzhou general and imperial commissioner and placed over Zhejiang maritime affairs.

sentences.zh: 因御史蘇廷魁奏英吉利為鄰國所破，詔促耆英赴廣州本任，乘機進剿，尋知其訛傳，仍留浙江。

translations.literal: Because Censor Su Tingkui memorialized that England had been defeated by neighboring states, an edict urged Qiying to proceed to his Guangzhou post and seize the chance to attack; soon the report proved false and he remained in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Su Tingkui reported that Britain had been beaten by its neighbors, and the court urged Qiying to take his Guangzhou post and strike while the chance remained. The report proved false, and he stayed in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 五月，吳淞失守，命偕伊里布赴江蘇相機籌辦。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Wusong fell; he was ordered to join Yi Libu in Jiangsu to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Wusong fell. He was ordered to join Yi Libu in Jiangsu and act as circumstances allowed.

sentences.zh: 英兵已入江，越圌山關，陷鎮江，踞瓜洲，耆英與揚威將軍奕經先後奏請羈縻招撫。

translations.literal: British troops had entered the Yangtze, passed Mount Tu, taken Zhenjiang, and held Guazhou; Qiying and Pacification General Yijing successively memorialized requesting temporizing pacification.
translations.idiomatic: British troops had entered the Yangtze, passed Mount Tu, taken Zhenjiang, and held Guazhou. Qiying and Pacification General Yijing both asked to temporize and pacify.

sentences.zh: 七月，英兵薄江寧下關，伊里布先至，英人索煙價、商欠、戰費共二千一百萬兩，廣州、福州、廈門、寧波、上海五港通商，英官與中國官員用平行禮，及劃抵關稅、釋放漢奸等款。

translations.literal: In the seventh month British troops approached Xiaguan at Jiangning; Yi Libu arrived first. The English demanded twenty-one million taels for opium indemnity, merchant debts, and war costs; trade at five ports—Guangzhou, Fuzhou, Xiamen, Ningbo, and Shanghai; parallel ceremonial status for British and Chinese officials; and provisions on offsetting customs duties and releasing Han traitors.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month British forces approached Xiaguan at Jiangning. Yi Libu arrived first. The British demanded twenty-one million taels for opium indemnity, merchant debts, and war costs; trade at Guangzhou, Fuzhou, Xiamen, Ningbo, and Shanghai; equal ceremonial status for British and Chinese officials; and terms on customs offsets and release of Han collaborators.

sentences.zh: 越三日，耆英至，稍稍駁詰之。

translations.literal: Three days later Qiying arrived and mildly disputed the terms.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later Qiying arrived and raised mild objections.

sentences.zh: 英兵突張紅旗，置砲鍾山上臨城，急止之，遣侍衛咸齡、江寧布政使恩彤、寧紹台道鹿澤良，偕伊里布家丁張喜，詣英舟，許據情奏聞。

translations.literal: The British suddenly raised a red flag and placed guns on Bell Mountain overlooking the city; he urgently stopped them and sent Bodyguard Xianling, Jiangning Provincial Treasurer Entong, Ning-Shao-Tai Circuit Intendant Lu Zeliang, together with Yi Libu's servant Zhang Xi, to the British ships, promising to memorialize according to the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The British suddenly raised a red flag and mounted guns on Bell Mountain overlooking the city. He stopped them urgently and sent Bodyguard Xianling, Jiangning Treasurer Entong, Circuit Intendant Lu Zeliang, and Yi Libu's servant Zhang Xi to the British ships, promising to report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 宣宗憤甚，大學士穆彰阿以糜餉勞師無效、剿與撫費亦相等為言，乃允之。

translations.literal: The Daoguang Emperor was greatly angered, but Grand Secretary Muzhanga argued that wasting funds on an ineffective campaign cost as much as pacification, and consent was given.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoguang Emperor was furious, but Grand Secretary Muzhanga argued that the cost of a failing war equaled that of peace, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 耆英等與英將濮鼎查、馬利遜會盟於儀鳳門外靜海寺，同籤條約，先予六百萬，餘分三年給，和議遂成。

translations.literal: Qiying and others met the British generals Pottinger and Morrison in alliance at Jinghai Temple outside Yifeng Gate, signed the treaty together, gave six million first with the rest over three years, and peace was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Qiying and others met the British generals Pottinger and Morrison at Jinghai Temple outside Yifeng Gate, signed the treaty, paid six million taels at once with the rest over three years, and peace was made.

sentences.zh: 九月，英兵盡數駛出吳淞，授兩江總督，命籌辦通商及浙江、福建因地制宜之策。

translations.literal: In the ninth month all British troops sailed out of Wusong; he was appointed Two Jiangs governor-general and ordered to arrange trade and policies suited to local conditions in Zhejiang and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month all British forces left Wusong. He was made governor-general of the Two Jiangs and ordered to organize trade and local policies for Zhejiang and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，授欽差大臣，赴廣東議通商章程，就粵海關稅則分別增減，各口按新例一體開關，臚列整頓稅務條款，下廷議施行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was appointed imperial commissioner and sent to Guangdong to negotiate trade regulations; at the Guangdong Customs he adjusted tariffs up and down; every port opened under the new rules alike; he set out clauses to reform taxation and submitted them for court deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 23 he was named imperial commissioner and sent to Guangdong to negotiate trade rules, adjusted Guangdong Customs tariffs, opened every port under the new regulations, listed tax reforms, and submitted them for court approval.

sentences.zh: 又奏美利堅、法蘭西等國一體通商，允之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that the United States, France, and other countries should trade on the same terms; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the United States, France, and others trade on the same terms, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 美國請入京瞻覲，卻不許。

translations.literal: The United States requested an audience in the capital; this was refused.
translations.idiomatic: The United States asked for an imperial audience in the capital, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，調授兩廣總督，兼辦通商事宜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred and appointed Two Guangs governor-general, also handling trade affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 24 he was transferred to governor-general of the Two Guangs and also placed in charge of trade.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，協辦大學士，留總督任。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he became associate grand secretary while retaining the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 25 he was made associate grand secretary while keeping his post as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 比利時、丹麥等國請通商，命體察約束。

translations.literal: Belgium, Denmark, and other states requested trade; he was ordered to investigate and impose constraints.
translations.idiomatic: Belgium, Denmark, and others asked to trade, and he was told to investigate and set limits.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，京察，以殫心竭慮坐鎮海疆，被議敘。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, at the capital inspection, for devoting heart and strength to holding the maritime frontier, he received a merit citation.
translations.idiomatic: At the Daoguang 26 metropolitan review he earned a merit citation for devoting himself to the maritime frontier.

sentences.zh: 疏上練兵事宜，繕呈唐臣陸贄守備事宜狀，請下各將軍督撫置諸座右。

translations.literal: He memorialized on troop training, transcribed the Tang official Lu Zhi's 'Memorial on Garrison Affairs,' and asked that it be sent to every general and governor for placement at their desks.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on training troops, copied Lu Zhi's Tang memorial on garrison affairs, and asked that every general and governor keep it at hand.

sentences.zh: 英國請於西藏定界通商，諭耆英堅守成約，毋為搖惑。

translations.literal: Britain requested demarcation and trade in Tibet; Qiying was instructed to hold firmly to existing treaties and not be swayed.
translations.idiomatic: Britain asked to demarcate borders and trade in Tibet. Qiying was told to hold to existing treaties and not be moved.

sentences.zh: 故事，廣東洋商居住澳門，貿易有定界，赴洋行發貨，不得擅入省城。

translations.literal: By precedent Guangdong foreign merchants lived in Macao, trade had fixed bounds, goods were issued through the hong, and they might not enter the provincial city without permission.
translations.idiomatic: By long custom foreign merchants in Guangdong lived in Macao, traded within fixed limits through the hongs, and could not enter the provincial city at will.

sentences.zh: 自江寧和議有省城設立棧房及領事入城之約，粵民猶持舊例，愬於大吏，不省，乃舉團練，眾議洶洶，不受官吏約束。

translations.literal: Since the Jiangning peace provided for warehouses in the provincial city and consuls entering the city, Guangdong people still held to the old practice, complained to high officials without being understood, then raised militia; public opinion seethed and would not accept official restraint.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanjing treaty allowed warehouses in the provincial city and consuls to enter the city, but Guangdong people clung to old custom, appealed to high officials in vain, then formed militia. Public anger boiled over beyond official control.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，濮鼎查將入城，粵民不可，逡巡去。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Pottinger was about to enter the city; the people of Guangdong would not allow it, and he withdrew after hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 23 Pottinger was about to enter the city, but Guangdong people blocked him and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，英船復至，耆英遣廣州知府餘保純詣商，粵民鼓譟，安撫乃罷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year British ships returned; Qiying sent Guangzhou Prefect Yu Baochun to negotiate with the merchants; the people of Guangdong clamored, and only after pacification did matters subside.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 25 British ships returned. Qiying sent Guangzhou Prefect Yu Baochun to deal with the merchants, but Guangdong people raised an uproar that subsided only after pacification.

sentences.zh: 英人以登岸每遭窘辱，貽書大吏誚讓，群情憤激，不可曉諭。

translations.literal: The English, humiliated whenever they came ashore, sent letters of reproach to high officials; popular feeling was furious and could not be persuaded.
translations.idiomatic: The British, humiliated whenever they landed, wrote reproaches to high officials. Public anger was too fierce to reason with.

sentences.zh: 至二十七年，英船突入省河，要求益堅，耆英謾許兩年後踐約，始退，自請議處。

translations.literal: By the twenty-seventh year British ships suddenly entered the provincial river; their demands grew firmer; Qiying vaguely promised fulfillment in two years before they withdrew, and asked to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: By Daoguang 27 British ships suddenly entered the provincial river with harder demands. Qiying vaguely promised entry in two years before they withdrew, then asked to be punished.

sentences.zh: 諭嚴為防備，務出萬全。

translations.literal: He was instructed to prepare defenses strictly and ensure complete security.
translations.idiomatic: He was told to prepare defenses strictly and leave nothing to chance.

sentences.zh: 耆英知終必有釁。

translations.literal: Qiying knew trouble would come in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Qiying knew conflict would come in the end.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，請入覲，留京供職，賜雙眼花翎，管理禮部、兵部，兼都統。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he requested an audience, remained in the capital on duty, was granted the double-eyed peacock feather, and placed in charge of the Ministries of Rites and War while also serving as commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 28 he asked for an audience, stayed in the capital on duty, received the double-eyed peacock feather, and was placed over the Ministries of Rites and War while also serving as commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 尋拜文淵閣大學士，命赴山東查辦鹽務，校閱浙江營伍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, ordered to investigate salt affairs in Shandong, and to review the Zhejiang army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, sent to investigate salt affairs in Shandong, and to inspect the Zhejiang army.

sentences.zh: 三十年，文宗即位，應詔陳言，略曰：「求治莫先於用人、理財、行政諸大端。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, when the Wenzong Emperor ascended the throne, he responded to the edict calling for memorials, saying in summary: 'In seeking good government nothing comes before the great matters of employing men, managing finances, and administering affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 30, when the Wenzong Emperor took the throne, he responded to the call for memorials, writing in part: 'Good government begins with employing the right men, managing finances, and running administration.

sentences.zh: 用人之道，明試以功。

translations.literal: The way to employ men is to test them clearly by achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Men should be tested clearly by what they accomplish.

sentences.zh: 人有剛柔，才有長短。

translations.literal: Men differ in firmness and softness; talents differ in length and shortness.
translations.idiomatic: Men differ in temperament; talents differ in scope.

sentences.zh: 用違其才，君子亦恐誤事；

translations.literal: Use a man against his talent and even a gentleman may fail in the task;
translations.idiomatic: Use a man against his talents and even a gentleman may fail;

sentences.zh: 用得其當，小人亦能濟事。

translations.literal: use him fittingly and even a petty man can accomplish the work.
translations.idiomatic: use him rightly and even a petty man can get the work done.

sentences.zh: 設官分職，非為眾人藏身之地。

translations.literal: Offices are established and duties divided, not to provide hiding places for the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Offices exist to divide labor, not to give everyone a place to hide.

sentences.zh: 實心任事者，雖小人當保全；

translations.literal: Whoever serves in earnest should be kept, though he be a petty man;
translations.idiomatic: Whoever serves in earnest should be kept, even if he is a petty man;

sentences.zh: 不肯任怨者，雖君子當委置。

translations.literal: whoever will not bear responsibility should be set aside, though he be a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: whoever will not bear responsibility should be set aside, even if he is a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 行政在於得人，迂腐之說，無裨時務，泥古之論，難合機宜，財非人不理。

translations.literal: Administration lies in getting the right men; pedantic talk does not help current affairs; antiquarian argument does not suit the moment; finances cannot be managed without men.
translations.idiomatic: Administration depends on the right men. Pedantry does not help the times, antiquarianism does not fit circumstances, and finances cannot be managed without capable men.

sentences.zh: 今賦額四千餘萬，支用有餘，不能如額，以致短絀。

translations.literal: Today the tax quota is more than forty million, expenditures should leave a surplus, yet collection falls short of quota and produces a deficit.
translations.idiomatic: The tax quota now exceeds forty million taels and should leave a surplus, yet collection falls short and creates deficits.

sentences.zh: 致絀之由，非探本窮源，不能通盤清釐。

translations.literal: The causes of deficit cannot be cleared comprehensively without tracing them to the root.
translations.idiomatic: The causes of deficit cannot be cleared without tracing them to the root.

sentences.zh: 與其正賦外別費經營，不如於正賦中覈實籌畫。

translations.literal: Rather than spending extra effort outside the regular tax, it is better to plan realistically within the regular tax itself.'
translations.idiomatic: Rather than spending extra effort outside regular taxes, it is better to plan realistically within them.'

sentences.zh: 」疏入，特諭曰：「身為端揆，一言一動，舉朝所矜式。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, a special edict said: 'As chief minister, every word and act is a model for the whole court.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, a special edict said: 'As chief minister, every word and act is a model for the whole court.

sentences.zh: 耆英率意敷陳，持論過偏，顯違古訓，流弊曷可勝言。

translations.literal: Qiying spoke at will; his argument was too one-sided, plainly contrary to ancient teaching, and the evils that may flow from it are beyond telling.
translations.idiomatic: Qiying spoke rashly, his argument was too one-sided, plainly contrary to ancient teaching, and the harm it may cause is beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 」傳旨申飭。

translations.literal: ' An order was transmitted rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: ' A rebuke was transmitted.

sentences.zh: 耆英不自安，屢稱病。

translations.literal: Qiying felt ill at ease and repeatedly claimed illness.
translations.idiomatic: Qiying felt uneasy and repeatedly claimed illness.

sentences.zh: 是年十月，上手詔揭示穆彰阿及耆英罪狀，斥「耆英在廣東抑民奉夷，謾許入城，幾致不測之變。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year the emperor personally issued an edict revealing the crimes of Muzhanga and Qiying, condemning: 'Qiying in Guangdong suppressed the people and favored the foreigners, falsely promised entry to the city, and nearly brought on unforeseen disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year the emperor personally issued an edict revealing the crimes of Muzhanga and Qiying, condemning Qiying for suppressing the people and favoring foreigners in Guangdong, falsely promising entry to the city, and nearly causing disaster.

sentences.zh: 數面陳夷情可畏，應事周旋，但圖常保祿位。

translations.literal: He repeatedly told the court in person that foreign power was fearsome, dealt with affairs by temporizing, and sought only to keep his salary and rank.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly told the court the foreigners were fearsome, temporized in every affair, and sought only to keep his salary and rank.

sentences.zh: 穆彰阿暗而難明，耆英顯而易見，貽害國家，其罪則一」。

translations.literal: Muzhanga is hidden and hard to discern; Qiying is obvious at a glance; both harm the state, and their crime is one.'
translations.idiomatic: Muzhanga is hidden and hard to see through; Qiying is obvious; both harmed the state, and their crime was the same.'

sentences.zh: 猶念其迫於時勢，從寬降為部屬。

translations.literal: Still mindful that he was pressed by the times, the court leniently demoted him to a subordinate post.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful that he had been pressed by circumstances, the court leniently demoted him to a subordinate post.

sentences.zh: 尋補工部員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was reappointed assistant department director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed assistant director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，粵匪北犯，耆英子馬蘭鎮總兵慶錫奏請父子兄弟同赴軍前，命耆英隨巡防王大臣效力，以捐餉予四品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng the Guangdong rebels invaded northward; Qiying's son, Malan Town Brigadier Qingxi, memorialized asking that father, sons, and brothers go together to the front; Qiying was ordered to serve with the patrol grand ministers, and for contributing funds was given fourth-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3 the Taiping rebels pushed north. Qiying's son, Brigadier Qingxi of Malan Town, asked that father and sons serve together at the front. Qiying was ordered to serve with the patrol grand ministers and received fourth-rank insignia for donating supplies.

sentences.zh: 五年，慶錫向屬員借貸被劾，耆英坐私告，革職圈禁。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Qingxi was impeached for borrowing from subordinates; Qiying was punished for private denunciation, stripped of office, and placed under house arrest.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 5 Qingxi was impeached for borrowing from subordinates. Qiying was punished for private accusations, stripped of office, and confined.

sentences.zh: 八年，英人糾合法、美、俄諸國兵船犯天津，爭改條約，命大學士桂良、尚書花沙納扆往查辦。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the English gathered French, American, and Russian warships to attack Tianjin and pressed to revise the treaty; Grand Secretary Guiliang and Minister Huashana were ordered to proceed and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 8 Britain gathered French, American, and Russian warships against Tianjin and pressed to revise the treaty. Grand Secretary Guiliang and Minister Huashana were sent to investigate.

sentences.zh: 巡防王大臣薦耆英熟悉情形，召對，自陳原力任其難，予侍郎銜，赴天津協議。

translations.literal: The patrol grand ministers recommended Qiying as familiar with the situation; he was summoned for audience, declared himself willing to bear the hardship, was given vice-president rank, and sent to Tianjin to negotiate.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol grand ministers recommended Qiying as familiar with the situation. Summoned to audience, he said he was willing to bear the hardship, received vice-president rank, and was sent to negotiate at Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 初耆英之在廣東也，五口通商事多由裁決，一意遷就。

translations.literal: When Qiying had been in Guangdong, matters of trade at the five ports were largely decided by him, and he yielded on every point.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiying had been in Guangdong, he had largely decided trade matters at the five ports himself and yielded on every point.

sentences.zh: 七年冬，廣州陷，檔案為英人所得，譯出耆英章奏，多掩飾不實，深惡之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year Guangzhou fell; archives were taken by the English, and Qiying's memorials were translated—many concealed the truth, and they hated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Xianfeng 7 Guangzhou fell. The British seized the archives and translated Qiying's memorials, many of which concealed the truth. They hated him deeply.

sentences.zh: 及至天津，英人拒不見，惶恐求去，不候旨，回通州，於是欺謾之跡益彰，為王大臣論劾，嚴詔逮治，賜自盡。

translations.literal: When he reached Tianjin the English refused to see him; in fear he begged to leave, returned to Tongzhou without awaiting orders, and thus his deceit became still plainer; the grand ministers impeached him, a stern edict ordered his arrest, and he was granted suicide.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianjin the British refused to see him. In fear he begged to leave, returned to Tongzhou without waiting for orders, and his deceit became plain. Grand ministers impeached him, a stern edict ordered his arrest, and he was granted suicide.

sentences.zh: 論曰：罷戰言和，始發於琦善，去備媚敵，致敗之由。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The call to cease fighting and sue for peace began with Qi Shan; abandoning preparations and courting the enemy was the cause of defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: The turn to truce began with Qi Shan. Abandoning defenses and courting the enemy was what led to defeat.

sentences.zh: 伊里布有忍辱負重之心，無安危定傾之略，且廟謨未定，廷議紛紜，至江寧城下之盟，乃與耆英結束和議，損威喪權，貽害莫挽。

translations.literal: Yi Libu had a heart willing to endure humiliation and bear heavy burdens, but no strategy to secure safety or turn crisis aside; moreover court policy was unsettled and court debate was divided; by the time of the treaty beneath the walls of Jiangning, he and Qiying concluded the peace, diminishing prestige and forfeiting authority, with harm that could not be retrieved.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Libu was willing to endure humiliation but lacked a strategy to save the state. Court policy was unsettled and debate divided. By the treaty beneath Jiangning's walls he and Qiying concluded peace, diminishing prestige and forfeiting authority in ways that could not be undone.

sentences.zh: 耆英獨任善後，留廣州入城之隙，兵釁再開，浸致庚申之禍。

translations.literal: Qiying alone bore postwar arrangements, left the opening for entry into Guangzhou city, fighting broke out again, and gradually led to the disaster of Gengshen.
translations.idiomatic: Qiying alone handled the aftermath, left the opening for foreigners to enter Guangzhou city, fighting broke out again, and gradually led to the Gengshen disaster.

sentences.zh: 三人者同受惡名，而耆英不保其身命，宜哉。

translations.literal: All three bore the same evil reputation, yet Qiying alone did not preserve his life—as was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: All three earned the same ill repute, yet only Qiying failed to preserve his life—as was fitting.
